speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what training and assistance are provided to prison officers to equip them to handle prison inmates who have intellectual disability; and (b) what measures are put in place for such prison inmates to seek help in the event of any abuse or mistreatment by others around them.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what are the specific support programmes available for prison inmates with intellectual disability during their incarceration, especially when they have difficulties being separated from their caregivers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The training also familiarises the officers with the support structures available for such inmates within the prison system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Prison officers cannot be and are not trained to the level of qualified counsellors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Special needs will have to be dealt with by accessing specialist expertise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: MDT comprises professionals and specialists like psychiatrists, prison psychologists, prison correctional rehabilitation specialists and prison officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: MDT decides on the behavioural management plans for inmates with mental and intellectual disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Inmates may also raise requests or complaints with the Superintendent of their Institutions or with the Visiting Justices during their regular visits.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, SPS officers are trained to spot signs of inmate abuse when conducting their regular patrols and body searches.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Any inmate who commits offences against other inmates would be subjected to investigation and, if found guilty, punished.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, on a day-to-day basis, watching out for these, which is separate and distinct from the way that the officers would watch over the other prisoners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If there are certain needs that need to be provided or we be mindful of, we will certainly do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: On a day-to-day basis, you will realise that even though our ex-offenders have made mistakes in their life, there is a lot of element of care within the Correctional Unit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I feel very touched sometimes when I visit the prison.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Fellow inmates, they share with me, they care for one another and they look out for one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What they want is to go through a holistic process or throughcare process of rehabilitation and reintegration for each and every one of them, including those with intellectual disability.
